_comment: Tier criteria in the words Jev sees. Keep them consistent with ROUTING.md; they are the Choice criteria of every routing question.

tiers.haiku: Read-only watching and status: waiting on a pipeline, job, merge request, shell or agent; reading a failure reason or log tail; listing branches or worktrees; grepping logs. No editing, no judgement.
tiers.sonnet: Mechanical or bounded work with a clear spec: commit, push, pull, rebase, merge; status reports and handoff summaries; bounded web sweeps and probes; fetching assets or logos; persona, prose and consistency reviews; UI, slide or CSS micro-edits with exact instructions; fixing tests that drifted after a known change; Linux or hardware troubleshooting; quick how-to questions; distilling docs.
tiers.opus: Work that needs judgement: implementing a feature or extraction logic; planning; orchestrating a campaign; architecture; content and argument work; synthesis across sources; acting as jury or verifier of others' work; hard design.

routes.keep: Needs the main session itself: a design decision, a judgement call, a question to the assistant, a reply to something it asked, a multi-step task that depends on what is already in this conversation, or an instruction about how to work.
routes.ship: Commit and/or push the current work.
routes.status-report: Pull the latest changes and report where a repository stands.
routes.ci-watcher: Wait for or check a pipeline, job, merge request, background shell or agent, and report its state.
routes.sysadmin: A problem with this Linux workstation: displays, docks, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, audio, fans, freezes, suspend, package installs, Docker Desktop, disks, USB, boot.
routes.sweeper: A bounded research or extraction batch: probe a list of sites, importers or catalogues for fields, find official sources or price lists, fetch logos, distill a set of docs.
routes.mechanic: Apply an already-decided change with exact instructions: a CSS or slide tweak, a rename, a small refactor, a test fix after a known change.
routes.reviewer: Review a document, deck, report or page through a stated lens: a reader persona, clarity, jargon, consistency of terms or numbers.
